commit.message:
chore(release): unify app version behind backend/VERSION

The app version was scattered across four independently hand-maintained
copies (backend/app/version.py's default, backend/pyproject.toml,
frontend-enterprise/package.json, and packaging fallback defaults), none
of which had been updated since project inception (still 0.1.0) while
git tags had moved on to v0.5.2. There was no single source of truth.

- backend/VERSION is now the single source of truth (bare semver, no
  `v` prefix). It lives under backend/ because setuptools' dynamic
  version resolution refuses to read a file outside its project root.
- backend/pyproject.toml reads it dynamically via
  [tool.setuptools.dynamic]; its static `version` field is gone.
- backend/app/version.py's fallback default now reads backend/VERSION
  instead of a hardcoded string.
- packaging/build_{macos,linux}.sh and build_windows.ps1 fall back to
  backend/VERSION when the caller doesn't pass VERSION explicitly.
- frontend-enterprise/package.json can't read the file directly (no
  such npm mechanism), so scripts/sync_version.py copies the value in;
  running it is documented as part of the release flow in AGENTS.md.
- release.yml now fails the build if the pushed tag or package.json
  don't match backend/VERSION, so a missed sync or a mistyped tag
  blocks shipping instead of silently drifting.
- AGENTS.md documents the release flow and SemVer classification
  rules (with a pre-1.0 note: breaking changes bump minor, not major,
  until a deliberate 1.0.0 milestone).

Testing:
- backend: `pytest` — 2010 passed
- `python -c "from app import version; ..."` confirms app_version()
  resolves backend/VERSION correctly
- `uv build --wheel` and `uv pip install -e .` confirm
  backend/pyproject.toml's dynamic version resolves correctly
  (verified by changing backend/VERSION and rebuilding)
- `scripts/sync_version.py` verified idempotent and correctly updates
  frontend-enterprise/package.json
- bash -n on the three edited shell scripts; PyYAML parse of the
  edited workflow file
- packaging/build_windows.ps1 reviewed manually only — no pwsh
  available in this environment

@@ -33,6 +33,22 @@ jobs:
     steps:
       - uses: actions/checkout@v7
 
+      - name: Validate tag and package.json match backend/VERSION
+        if: github.event_name != 'workflow_dispatch'
+        shell: bash
+        run: |
+          tag_version="${GITHUB_REF_NAME#v}"
+          file_version="$(cat backend/VERSION)"
+          if [ "$tag_version" != "$file_version" ]; then
+            echo "::error::tag $GITHUB_REF_NAME does not match backend/VERSION ($file_version). Fix VERSION and re-tag."
+            exit 1
+          fi
+          pkg_version="$(grep -m1 '"version"' frontend-enterprise/package.json | sed -E 's/.*"version": *"([^"]*)".*/\1/')"
+          if [ "$pkg_version" != "$file_version" ]; then
+            echo "::error::frontend-enterprise/package.json ($pkg_version) does not match backend/VERSION ($file_version). Run scripts/sync_version.py, commit, and re-tag."
+            exit 1
+          fi
+
       - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
         with:
           node-version: "20"

@@ -30,6 +30,23 @@ Follow the history’s concise Conventional Commit pattern, such as `feat(channe

+## Release & Versioning
+
+`backend/VERSION` (bare semver, no `v` prefix) is the single source of truth for the app version.
+`backend/pyproject.toml` reads it dynamically — never hand-edit its `version` field.
+`frontend-enterprise/package.json` can't read it (no such npm mechanism), so run
+`scripts/sync_version.py` in the same commit whenever you edit `backend/VERSION`; `release.yml`
+fails the build if it drifts.
+
+Only bump `backend/VERSION` when preparing a release, not on routine PRs — parallel
+branches/worktrees would conflict on it otherwise. Classify the most severe change since the last
+tag: patch = compatible bug fix only, minor = new backward-compatible functionality, major =
+breaking change — except pre-1.0 (current line `0.x.y`), where breaking changes bump minor instead
+and major is reserved for a deliberate `1.0.0` milestone.
+
+Flow: edit `backend/VERSION` → run `scripts/sync_version.py` → commit → merge → `git tag vX.Y.Z`
+(must match the file) → `git push --tags`.
+

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Propagate backend/VERSION into files that can't read it directly.
+
+Run this once, as the last step before tagging a release, after backend/VERSION
+has been edited to the new version number:
+
+    scripts/sync_version.py
+
+backend/pyproject.toml reads backend/VERSION directly (setuptools dynamic
+version) and needs no sync. frontend-enterprise/package.json can't — npm has
+no mechanism to read a version from an external file — so this script copies
+the value in. CI (.github/workflows/release.yml) fails the release build if
+package.json ever drifts from backend/VERSION, so a forgotten run here is
+caught before it ships, not silently.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import re
+import sys
+from pathlib import Path
+
+REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
+
+
+def read_version() -> str:
+    value = (REPO / "backend" / "VERSION").read_text(encoding="utf-8").strip()
+    if not value:
+        raise SystemExit("backend/VERSION is empty")
+    return value
+
+
+def sync_package_json(version: str) -> bool:
+    path = REPO / "frontend-enterprise" / "package.json"
+    text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
+    new_text, count = re.subn(
+        r'"version": "[^"]*"', f'"version": "{version}"', text, count=1
+    )
+    if count == 0:
+        raise SystemExit(f"could not find a version field in {path}")
+    if new_text == text:
+        return False
+    path.write_text(new_text, encoding="utf-8")
+    return True
+
+
+def main() -> int:
+    version = read_version()
+    if sync_package_json(version):
+        print(f"synced {version} into frontend-enterprise/package.json")
+    else:
+        print(f"already in sync at {version}")
+    return 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(main())

## Summary
The app version was scattered across four independently hand-maintained copies (`backend/app/version.py`'s default, `backend/pyproject.toml`, `frontend-enterprise/package.json`, and packaging fallback defaults), none updated since project inception (still `0.1.0`) while git tags had moved on to `v0.5.2`. This introduces a single source of truth.

## Changes
- `backend/VERSION` is the single source of truth (bare semver, no `v` prefix). It lives under `backend/` because setuptools' dynamic version resolution refuses to read a file outside its project root.
- `backend/pyproject.toml` reads it dynamically via `[tool.setuptools.dynamic]`; its static `version` field is removed.
- `backend/app/version.py`'s fallback default now reads `backend/VERSION` instead of a hardcoded string.
- `packaging/build_{macos,linux}.sh` and `build_windows.ps1` fall back to `backend/VERSION` when the caller doesn't pass `VERSION` explicitly.
- `frontend-enterprise/package.json` can't read the file directly (no such npm mechanism), so `scripts/sync_version.py` copies the value in; running it is documented as part of the release flow in `AGENTS.md`.
- `release.yml` now fails the build if the pushed tag or `package.json` don't match `backend/VERSION`, so a missed sync or a mistyped tag blocks shipping instead of silently drifting.
- `AGENTS.md` documents the release flow and SemVer classification rules (pre-1.0 note: breaking changes bump minor, not major, until a deliberate `1.0.0` milestone).

## Testing
- `pytest` (backend): 2010 passed
- `python -c "from app import version; ..."` confirms `app_version()` resolves `backend/VERSION` correctly
- `uv build --wheel` and `uv pip install -e .` confirm `backend/pyproject.toml`'s dynamic version resolves correctly (verified by changing `backend/VERSION` and rebuilding)
- `scripts/sync_version.py` verified idempotent and correctly updates `frontend-enterprise/package.json`
- `bash -n` on the three edited shell scripts; PyYAML parse of the edited workflow file

## Risks
- `packaging/build_windows.ps1` was reviewed manually only — no `pwsh` available to actually execute it in this environment.
- Whether GitHub Actions can push (`sync_version.py`-driven fixes are manual, not automated, so this isn't applicable here) — not a risk for this PR since there's no bot-push workflow.
- No functional runtime change: `backend/pyproject.toml`'s `version` field and `frontend-enterprise/package.json`'s `version` field are not read anywhere else in the codebase (verified by search), so this is packaging/release-process only.
